title: String-based algorithm identification prevents ABI lock-in
description: Algorithm names are null-terminated strings throughout the UAPI (algo field in crypto2dev_init_op, crypto2dev_key_import_op, crypto2dev_kdf_op, etc.). Provider names are strings. There are no enum values or integer algorithm IDs in any ioctl struct. The UAPI header states this explicitly: 'No enums, no flags. Algorithm names are strings. New behaviors get new ioctls or new named fields, never a new bit in a flags word.' String-based identifiers allow new algorithms (including post-quantum) to be added without any change to the kernel header — existing userspace binaries continue to work, and new userspace binaries can request new algorithm names without recompiling the kernel or any other userspace binary. A reviewer might argue for an enum or integer ID for 'efficiency' or 'type safety.' That would freeze the algorithm namespace at compile time and create permanent ABI debt: any new algorithm requires a header change and recompile of every caller, including out-of-tree modules that cannot be recompiled. The string approach has negligible cost — strcmp on a 64-byte field at session open time is not on any hot path.
close_reason: Design decision confirmed by code inspection — no code change required.
